content: Spouses married under community property, separated by final judgment. Wife sought dissolution and division of jointly-owned garage property in Jesi. Husband agreed but claimed wife enjoyed exclusive use, seeking compensation. Articles 191, 1111 Italian Civil Code and 784 et seq. Italian Code of Civil Procedure govern community dissolution timing and division procedures. Issue concerned whether final separation judgment requirement satisfied for dissolution action. Personal separation (judicial/consensual) dissolution of community property finalizes only with final judgment or consensual separation approval—not presidential order per Article 708. Presidential orders are provisional, functionally limited, confer no dissolution effect. Final judgment constitutes event giving rise to dissolution right and creates concrete current interest in bringing action—qualifies as condition for action, not procedural requirement. Original deficiency becomes irrelevant when requirements fulfilled during proceedings—reflects procedural economy principle. Plaintiff initially alleged/demonstrated separation pronouncement; defendant confirmed judgment existence; plaintiff later demonstrated judgment finality at conclusions hearing. Dissolution declaratory in nature: acknowledges pre-existing pro rata ownership from joint ownership inception, creates no new rights. Party declarations regarding cadastral/regulatory correspondence superfluous given declaratory nature. Garage property divisible per court-appointed expert findings. Direct assignment made per expert division plan. Costs fully compensated between parties given declaratory nature.
